blocks.text: Quick verdict

Oxylabs is the better provider for large, steady scraping pipelines and hard targets: its 175M+ pool is more than five times IPRoyal's, its scraper APIs remove anti-bot work, and its rates fall to $2.50/GB on big plans. IPRoyal is the better choice for small teams, irregular projects and account management, because you can start with 1 GB, your traffic never expires, and sticky sessions run up to seven days. Below roughly 20 GB a month, IPRoyal is usually the more sensible spend.

Oxylabs and IPRoyal sit at opposite ends of the residential proxy market. Oxylabs is an enterprise provider with one of the two largest pools in the world, published 99.95% success rates and scraper APIs that bill per result. IPRoyal is a value provider whose residential traffic never expires and can be bought one gigabyte at a time. Comparing them is really a question of scale: at what point does Oxylabs' quality and tooling justify paying more, and when is IPRoyal simply the smarter buy?

blocks.text: Oxylabs in 2026: what you get

Oxylabs sells enterprise-grade proxy infrastructure with a strong reputation among large scraping teams. Its residential network is one of the two largest on the market (175M+ advertised IPs, 195 locations), targeting reaches city, ZIP and ASN level, and its scraper APIs bundle rendering and parsing so you buy results rather than gigabytes. The weak spot for smaller buyers is entry cost: pay-as-you-go runs $8/GB and the cheapest monthly rate needs a $2,500 commitment.

Strengths: One of the two largest residential pools available; Published 99.95% residential success rate; Strong scraper APIs that bill per result; Formal ethical-sourcing documentation for procurement. Weak spots: Expensive at low volume ($8/GB PAYG); Best rates need large monthly commitments; Residential trial goes through sales rather than self-service.
IPRoyal in 2026: what you get

IPRoyal is a value-focused provider best known for residential traffic that never expires. You can buy a single gigabyte, use it over months, and top up when you need to, which suits irregular projects better than monthly allowances. The residential pool is advertised at 32M+ IPs across 195 countries with state and city targeting, and sticky sessions can be requested for up to seven days. IPRoyal also sells ISP, datacenter and mobile proxies and a Web Unblocker billed per successful request.

Strengths: Residential traffic that does not expire; Sticky sessions up to 7 days; Can start with a single gigabyte; Several proxy types plus Web Unblocker in one account. Weak spots: Smaller pool than the enterprise networks; Headline $1.75/GB rate needs a 10 TB purchase; Mid-volume prices are not published.
Pricing: Oxylabs vs IPRoyal

Oxylabs charges $8/GB pay-as-you-go for residential traffic. Monthly plans start with Starter at $30 for 5 GB ($6/GB) and a Basic tier around $100 for 20 GB, and the rate falls to $2.50/GB on the $2,500/month Corporate plan. Mobile traffic starts at $7.50/GB.

IPRoyal's residential subscription costs $7 for 1 GB, $11.90 for 2 GB and $52.50 for 10 GB ($5.25/GB); pay-as-you-go is 5% more ($7.35 for 1 GB). The advertised $1.75/GB rate applies only at 10 TB. Prices for custom volumes such as 25, 100 or 500 GB are calculated in the dashboard.

For a 10 GB month, IPRoyal costs about $52.50 while Oxylabs costs about $80, so IPRoyal saves around 34%. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because Oxylabs and IPRoyal do not publish an exact price for that volume. Look past the per-GB figure too. IPRoyal lets unused traffic carry forward, while Oxylabs's allowance does not (monthly plan allowances reset each cycle). For irregular workloads, that difference can outweigh a small gap in list price.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

By advertised size, Oxylabs (175M+) is about 5.5x larger than IPRoyal (32M+). Advertised pool sizes are marketing figures counted over long periods; the number of IPs actually reachable in a given country at a given moment is far smaller for every provider, so treat these as a rough guide to depth rather than a guarantee. For coverage, Oxylabs lists 195 countries and IPRoyal lists 195. On targeting, Oxylabs offers country, state, city, ZIP and ASN, while IPRoyal offers country, state and city (ISP selection needs verification).
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, Oxylabs offers rotating and sticky sessions on residential and mobile, and IPRoyal offers rotating or sticky sessions from 1 second up to 7 days. Both use a backconnect gateway: you point your tool at one host and port, and choose country, city or session behaviour through parameters in the username.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: Oxylabs wins. The deciding factor for Oxylabs: its pool size and Web Scraper API suit large crawls. The limitation on the IPRoyal side: solid success rates and non-expiring traffic for bursty crawls.

SERP and rank tracking: Oxylabs wins. The deciding factor for Oxylabs: its scraper API returns parsed search results. The limitation on the IPRoyal side: it works, but it has no dedicated SERP product.

Social media and multi-account management: IPRoyal. IPRoyal has the edge here. Why: 7-day sticky sessions keep one IP on one account. How Oxylabs compares: it works, but the pricing is built for volume, not a handful of accounts.

E-commerce price and stock monitoring: Oxylabs wins. The deciding factor for Oxylabs: city and ZIP targeting plus parsed e-commerce endpoints. The limitation on the IPRoyal side: city targeting with pay-only-for-what-you-use traffic.

Ad verification and geo-testing: Oxylabs. Oxylabs has the edge here. Why: broad geo coverage with ASN targeting. How IPRoyal compares: decent coverage but no ASN or carrier targeting on standard accounts.
Tight budgets: IPRoyal. IPRoyal has the edge here. Why: small entry purchases and traffic that never expires. How Oxylabs compares: entry pricing is among the highest in this comparison.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. Oxylabs: Residential trial arranged through sales, once per customer. IPRoyal: No general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies. Verification and payment rules differ too. Oxylabs: Business verification on larger accounts. IPRoyal: Optional ID verification; required for ISP-level targeting and PayPal. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test Oxylabs and IPRoyal before you commit
Spec sheets only get you so far. A short, structured test on your own targets will settle Oxylabs vs IPRoyal faster than any review:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (Oxylabs: residential trial arranged through sales, once per customer; IPRoyal: no general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, Oxylabs comes out ahead in 4, IPRoyal in 2, and 0 are ties. That makes Oxylabs the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: Oxylabs is strongest for large scraping pipelines with steady volume, while IPRoyal is strongest for irregular or seasonal projects. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
